text:
RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 35

An all-male panel is weak evidence on its own. Structural engineering is heavily male-dominated, so a four-man panel is close to what random selection would produce — it's a fact about the profession more than about your interview. It matters mainly as context, not as proof.

Your stronger points are substantive: a large credential and experience gap, and a winning criterion ("excellent client relationships") that is vague, unmeasured, and the kind of soft judgement where bias most easily operates. Also the unanswered request — most employers owe reasons, and silence is itself worth pressing.

So: chase the written explanation firmly. Lead with the qualification gap and the undefined criterion. Mention panel composition as background only; leading with it invites dismissal.
